 Considered as an income of 600,000 won per person, tax collection
 The management requests a trial to the Tax Tribunal
 There is a concern that welfare will decrease when income is recognized 사진 확대 [Yonhap News] The National Tax Service and Samsung Group affiliates disagreed on whether the health examination expenses provided by the company to employees should be regarded as workers' income, leading to a legal dispute. When the National Tax Service imposed taxes on the entire health examination expenses provided by the company to employees as earned income, the management countered that "the cost of fulfilling the mandatory examination set by the law" and asked the Tax Tribunal for a trial. As many companies are providing health examination expenses to employees, it is expected that the results of the interpretation will inevitably have a big impact on companies and workers.
 According to the tax industry on the 8th, the National Tax Service determined that the health examination expenses supported by the company were earned income in a tax audit of Samsung Financial Group A conducted late last year and notified that it would collect about 660 million won in earned income tax attributable to 2022-2025. The company provides comprehensive examination expenses worth about 600,000 won per employee.
 In particular, it was confirmed that the National Tax Service included the legal examination in the taxable category. Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, general health checkups can be replaced by national health checkups conducted free of charge by the National Health Insurance Corporation, so the entire support cost of the management should be regarded as income.
 The management objected to this and requested a "pre-taxation denial review" to verify the adequacy of the taxation content before disposing of the tax notice, but the National Tax Service did not accept it. In response, the company requested a trial to the Tax Tribunal. The Tax Tribunal, a quasi (準) judicial body under the Prime Minister's Office, is in charge of administrative trials on tax disputes.
 In addition, it was found that corporation A also applied for an authoritative interpretation to the Ministry of Finance and Economy to clearly check whether support for health examination expenses for employees can be viewed as income.
 The reason for such confusion is that there is currently no clear detailed regulation on whether the health examination fee subsidy is viewed as worker income.
 If subsidies for health checkups are regarded as income, as the National Tax Service claims, the earned income tax that employees have to pay in the future will also increase. There are concerns that the company may also take on the rise in the burden of the four major insurance premium companies due to the inclusion of earned income, which could reduce welfare benefits for employees.
 On the contrary, if health examination expenses are not recognized as income, there is a possibility that companies that have withheld medical examination expenses will start the tax refund process.
 An official from the National Tax Service said, "We cannot confirm the details of the individual tax investigation."
 If the income of health examination expenses is recognized, it is included in the calculation of the four major insurances As the National Tax Service judged that the subsidies for health checkups by Samsung Group's financial affiliates were earned income, it is interpreted that the controversy over the taxation standard for in-house welfare benefits has risen to the surface.
 Under the current income tax law, the price for providing and receiving work is regarded as 'earned income' regardless of form. Non-taxable items are listed one by one, but health examination fees are not included in this list. If the legal phrase is interpreted as it is, there is room for it to be regarded as 'earned income'.
 사진 확대 However, the tax industry says that it has been customary not to regard health examination expenses supported by the company as income in the usual range. An official from a financial team at a large Korean company said, "As the support for health checkups is related to the 'right to health' of employees, the tax authorities did not consider it as income within a certain level, but Samsung's case is somewhat unusual."
 The National Tax Service also says it does not have accurate regulations, such as the amount of money, on whether or not to view the support for health examination expenses as income. In other words, there is much room for the "interpretation" and "discretion" of the investigator at the actual tax audit site. A tax accountant who requested anonymity said, "The tax judgment may vary depending on the company's internal regulations and the difference in the level of support between executives and employees." Another tax accountant said, "There is a lot of room for disagreement in interpretation as subjectivity can also be involved in the judgment of the scope of support for the appropriate screening."
 The biggest controversy in this dispute is that the National Tax Service judged that even compulsory examination expenses were subject to taxation. Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, employers are obligated to conduct health checkups for workers' health care. As the examination, which is a basic examination, is mandatory, it was common to view it as an expense for management needs rather than income.
 Samsung affiliates also argue that support for health checkups constitutes "expenditure by business necessity" as a key reason for objecting to the disposition of the National Tax Service.
 However, the National Tax Service determined that the amount of support for the examination provided by the management corresponds to the full "earned income" because it can be replaced by a free national health examination conducted by the National Health Insurance Service. It is a very strict interpretation of the scope of non-taxation of earned income. In addition, the fact that the check-up includes expensive check-ups such as CT scans and that it is specified as welfare benefits in the job posting is also the basis for considering it as earned income.
 An official from the National Tax Service said, "If there is no certain control over the welfare benefits provided by the company, there is a concern that the benefits will be covered and the salaries will be dispersed."
 사진 확대 [Yonhap News] Concerns over a reduction in welfare benefits if the company's burden increases On the other hand, the management confronts that the examination fee should be excluded from earned income based on the fact that it is directly paid to the hospital and cannot be used by employees personally. Earlier, the Supreme Court regarded the welfare points provided by the company to employees in 2024 as earned income and cited the fact that "you can freely purchase necessary goods and services within the set period and purpose." The management explains that examination support expenses do not meet these requirements.
 As opinions differ over the interpretation of the company's health examination support, different companies deal with it. Some companies withhold health examination support expenses for all executives and employees as earned income, while others regard it as income from high-value health examinations provided to some executives. Many companies do not regard the cost of health checkups as earned income at all.
 Moreover, Samsung Group affiliates are also operating different policies on whether or not to tax health checkups. In response, the National Tax Service reportedly emphasized the legitimacy of the taxation based on the case of other Samsung affiliates that consider health examination expenses as income.
 The results of the Tax Tribunal's judgment scheduled for next month are expected to eventually be a key issue whether the amount of support for examination expenses is outside the usual range. An official from the tax industry said, "The results of the trial will be a gauge of the appropriate level of support for examination expenses provided by the company."
 The impact of the referee's results is expected to be formidable. If the judges rule in favor of the National Tax Service, companies that support medical examination expenses in the same way are more likely to have to treat the amount as income. The same taxation logic is likely to be applied to other companies, a tax industry official said. "The tax burden on employees increases, and it could be an opportunity for companies to pay taxes or adjust the scope of examination support."
 Companies can impose additional taxes on the past portion of the withholding tax, and the burden of the four major insurance premium companies will also increase in the future. As such, there is an incentive to reduce subsidies from the company's point of view.
 Even if the management wins, it has an impact. This is because companies that have been withholding tax on subsidies for health checkups can request a correction to return the taxes they have already paid. However, the judge's decision is only effective in the case, and it is predicted that the Ministry of Finance's interpretation of the authority will eventually be the key.
